1.why: Text uses a clear, legible typeface with adequate spacing, but no explicit dyslexia-friendly font (e.g., OpenDyslexic) is visible.

2.why: No italics, all-caps, or dense text blocks are present; instructions are concise and well-formatted.

3.why: Content is readable and well laid out on mobile screens, with appropriate spacing and sizing.

4.why: Instructions are short, direct, and use plain language (e.g., 'Enter one unused recovery code').

5.why: Examples are provided for inputs (e.g., 'Example: ABCD-EFGH-JKLM' for recovery codes).

6.why: No step requires reading long blocks of text to proceed; instructions are broken into small, digestible chunks.

7.why: Long codes (e.g., recovery codes) can be copied via 'Copy all codes' button.

8.why: QR code is offered as an alternative to manual entry for authenticator setup (step_05).

9.why: No explicit evidence of autofill or password manager support, though fields are standard input types.

10.why: Primary actions (e.g., 'Set up authenticator', 'Confirm authenticator') stand out clearly with bold buttons.

11.why: Only one main action is requested per screen (e.g., 'Create recovery codes' or 'Check recovery code').

12.why: System confirms actions plainly (e.g., 'Authenticator confirmed. Now save your recovery codes.').

13.why: Users can retry steps (e.g., 'Use a recovery code' option) and reveal/hide codes (e.g., 'Hide recovery codes').

14.why: Error messages are clear (e.g., 'Your page check expired. Refresh the page and try again.') but lack explicit 'how to fix' guidance.

15.why: No time limits are imposed on reading or code entry; users can proceed at their own pace.
